e: The internal inguinal ring is an opening in the transversalis fascia, forming the posterior wall at this site.
The lateral pterygoid attaches to the articular disc and capsule of the temporomandibular joint.
The glomerulus is a tuft of fenestrated capillaries enclosed by Bowman's capsule.
The left 6th aortic arch forms the left pulmonary artery and, via its distal part, the ductus arteriosus.
The urachus becomes the median umbilical ligament after obliteration.
The common fibular nerve is vulnerable around the neck of the fibula; its deep fibular branch supplies dorsiflexors.
The greater auricular nerve supplies sensation over the skin around the angle of the mandible and parotid region, including the area below the ear lobule.

Pen test (thumb abducted against a pen) tests abductor pollicis brevis → median nerve.
Ulnar nerve: Card/Froment's test (adductor pollicis)

Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C7) supplies biceps, brachialis, coracobrachialis → elbow flexion & supination.
Its lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm gives lateral forearm sensation

Umbilical arteries (2) carry deoxygenated blood from fetus → placenta.
Umbilical vein (1) brings oxygenated blood to the fetus
Phrenicocolic ligament (diaphragm → splenic flexure) = 'sustentaculum lienis', supports the spleen & prevents its vertical descent
Gag reflex: afferent limb = CN IX (glossopharyngeal), efferent limb = CN X (vagus)
Great saphenous vein runs c̅ the saphenous nerve (branch of femoral) along the medial leg → injury gives medial leg & foot neuralgia

Jugular foramen transmits CN IX, X, XI (+ IJV).
Hypoglossal nerve leaves via the hypoglossal canal

PDA arises from the distal part of the left 6th aortic arch (ductus arteriosus), joining the pulmonary trunk to the aorta.
Right 6th arch → right pulmonary artery

Vagus has GVA, GVE, SVE, GSA and SVA fibres.
GSE is present only in CN III, IV, VI, XII

2nd, 3rd Phx Arch Muscle & Nerve Supply
Facial nerve → posterior belly of digastric & stylohyoid.
Nerve to mylohyoid (V3) →anterior belly of digastric & mylohyoid
Meralgia paresthetica = entrapment of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (L2–L3) under the inguinal ligament → anterolateral thigh paresthesia

Forceful eversion stretches/tears the deltoid (medial) ligament – the strongest ankle ligament.
Inversion injury → anterior talofibular ligament

Long head of triceps arises from the infraglenoid tubercle.
Supraglenoid tubercle = long head of biceps

Transitional epithelium (urothelium) c̅ dome-shaped umbrella cells lines the ureter, bladder & renal pelvis.
Gallbladder/intestine: simple columnar

Round ligament: pulls the fundus forward, maintaining the Anteversion.
Uterosacral: Pulls the cervix posteriorly, maintaining Anteflexion.
Cardinal: prevent Prolapse

Gluteus Maximus is Chief Extensor and lateral rotator of the hip joint.
It's Upper fibres (75%) inserts into iliotibial tract -> Abducts the thigh.
While Lower (25%) inserts into gluteal tuberosity -> assists in Adduction
Trapezius muscle shrugs 🤷 the shoulder & abducts arm above 90°, which is supplied by CN XI, which courses superficially within the posterior triangle

Intermediate mesoderm (nephrogenic cord) forms Urogenital system (kidney + ureter).
Paraxial mesoderm forms somites.
Allantois gives rise to the urachus

Wasting + ↓ tone = LMN lesion → anterior horn cell damage.
UMN lesions (pyramidal tract, internal capsule, corticospinal tract) → spasticity, ↑ tone
Marginal mandibular nerve (branch of facial) lies superficial to the submandibular gland → at risk in its excision; incision is placed below the mandible
